title: Salvage Value Basis for Owner-Retained Total-Loss Vehicles, Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage
content:
**Salvage guideline.** The salvage value on which the salvage deduction of a Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage kept-vehicle settlement rests is set as follows. Where more than 30 days have passed from the declaration date to the acceptance date, the salvage bid has lapsed and the salvage value is 30 percent of the actual cash value; where the bid is still valid but below 25 percent of the actual cash value, the salvage value is 25 percent of the actual cash value; otherwise the salvage value is the highest salvage bid. Each percentage figure is rounded to the cent.

The declaration date, the highest salvage bid and the actual cash value are read from the claim's total-loss declaration; the acceptance date is the date the customer accepts the kept-vehicle settlement.

| Days from declaration to acceptance | Highest salvage bid | Salvage value |
|---|---|---|
| More than 30 | Any (lapsed) | 30 percent of the actual cash value |
| 30 or fewer | Below 25 percent of the actual cash value | 25 percent of the actual cash value |
| 30 or fewer | 25 percent of the actual cash value or more | The highest salvage bid |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical figures, actual cash value 12000.00)

25 percent of the actual cash value is 3000.00; 30 percent is 3600.00.
- Accepted 30 days after the declaration, bid 3200.00: still valid and not below 3000.00, so 3200.00.
- Accepted 30 days after, bid 2500.00: below 3000.00, so 3000.00.
- Accepted 31 days after, bid 3200.00: lapsed, so 3600.00.
- Accepted 10 days after, bid exactly 3000.00: not below 25 percent, so 3000.00.
